name: std::sqrt(std::complex)
intro: Computes the square root of the complex number z with a branch cut along the negative real axis.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
z

 -

 complex number to take the square root of

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: If no errors occur, returns the square root of z, in the range of the right half-plane, including the imaginary axis ([0; +∞) along the real axis and (−∞; +∞) along the imaginary axis).

sections.title: Error handling and special values
sections.text:
Errors are reported consistent with math_errhandling.

If the implementation supports IEEE floating-point arithmetic,

The function is continuous onto the branch cut taking into account the sign of imaginary part
 std::sqrt(std::conj(z)) == std::conj(std::sqrt(z))
 If z is (±0,+0), the result is (+0,+0)
 If z is (x,+∞), the result is (+∞,+∞) even if x is NaN
 If z is (x,NaN), the result is (NaN,NaN) (unless x is ±∞) and  FE_INVALID may be raised
 If z is (-∞,y), the result is (+0,+∞) for finite positive y
 If z is (+∞,y), the result is (+∞,+0) for finite positive y
 If z is (-∞,NaN), the result is (NaN,∞) (sign of imaginary part unspecified)
 If z is (+∞,NaN), the result is (+∞,NaN)
 If z is (NaN,y), the result is (NaN,NaN) and FE_INVALID may be raised
 If z is (NaN,NaN), the result is (NaN,NaN)

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: The semantics of this function are intended to be consistent with the C function csqrt.

examples.output:
Square root of -4 is (0,2)
Square root of (-4,-0) is (0,-2) (the other side of the cut)

summary: Computes the square root of the complex number z with a branch cut along the negative real axis.
